display.purpose: Hero headlines and the 404 numeral only. Uppercase, 900, tight leading.

body.purpose: Default reading copy; article body at 17px/1.65 with a 720px measure.

body-large.purpose: Hero subtitles, page descriptions, intro paragraphs.

label.purpose: Machine-produced text: dates, counts, reading time, badges, chips.

code.purpose: Inline code, pre blocks, table headers, and small metadata runs in prose.

post-h3.purpose: Third-level headings inside article prose, below the 1.875rem H2 rule.

numeral.purpose: The 404 numeral and other single-glyph display moments.

shadows.name: brutal-xs
shadows.purpose: Resting state after a press, and the hover target for small controls.

shadows.name: brutal-sm
shadows.purpose: Small controls at rest: tags, social icons, share buttons, related-post cards.

shadows.name: brutal-md
shadows.purpose: Default for cards, panels, sidebar blocks, inputs, and icon buttons.

shadows.name: brutal-lg
shadows.purpose: Emphasis tier: featured cards, project cards, newsletter, article banners, readout panels.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The universal hover/press transition: translate toward the shadow while it shrinks one tier.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Section entrance: 20px rise with fade, used on home bands and list items.

motion.name: instrument-readout
motion.value: width .1s linear on the level meter
motion.purpose: The reading instrument's only motion: the meter tracks the scroll position directly, no easing, no flourish.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main action on a surface: Alert Magenta, square, presses into its shadow on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 900; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: -0.025em; color: #111111; background: #FF1493; border: 2px solid #111111; border-radius: 0; padding: 12px 24px; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #111111; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .15s ease, box-shadow .15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translate(3px, 3px); box-shadow: 1px 1px 0 #111111; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translate(5px, 5px); box-shadow: 1px 1px 0 #111111; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #00D9FF; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The paired alternative action: Panel White, same square shape and press behaviour.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 900; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: -0.025em; color: #111111; background: #FFFFFF; border: 2px solid #111111; border-radius: 0; padding: 12px 24px; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #111111; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .15s ease, box-shadow .15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { transform: translate(3px, 3px); box-shadow: 1px 1px 0 #111111; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translate(5px, 5px); box-shadow: 1px 1px 0 #111111; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #00D9FF; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Tag Chip

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Small monospace label for state: Caution Yellow for post tags and featured flags, Alert Magenta for the featured marker.

components.description: Panel White container with a 2px rule and Brutal MD shadow; the default surface for posts and projects.

Introducing This Blog

Why I rebuilt my blog with Astro, Tailwind CSS, and a deliberately loud neo-brutalist design.

components.name: Text Input

narrative.overview:
A calm operations console drawn on graph paper. The palette is loud on purpose — cyan, magenta, yellow, green read as instrument states, not decoration — but the system that carries them is disciplined: one container width, one border weight family, one shadow vocabulary, one accent per signal. Nothing on the page is ambient. Every surface is bounded by a black rule, every element sits on the grid, and every colored block is labelled in monospace. It should feel like a readout you trust at 3am, not a page that is trying to impress you.

Density is high and typographic, closer to a printed specification than a marketing page. Display type is set heavy and uppercase in Space Grotesk; metadata, counts, badges and labels are set in JetBrains Mono so they read as machine output rather than prose. Body copy is Inter at a comfortable measure. The system never softens: no blur, no gradient fill, no rounded corner, no drop shadow without an offset. Where the print aesthetic would normally be a costume, here it is load-bearing — a hard black rule around a card is also what tells you the card is a card.

The register is calm operations: bright signals, ordered layout, no ornament that does not carry information. The one confirmed rejection is muted low-contrast palettes — this system earns its calm from legibility and order, not from desaturation.
keyCharacteristics: Hard black rules (2–4px) bound every surface; nothing floats unboxed.
Solid offset shadows with zero blur; depth is displacement, not light.
Zero border-radius anywhere; corners are always square.
Colour is signal: each accent carries one recurring meaning and always ships a text label.
Monospace for anything that reads as data; display grotesk for anything that reads as a heading.
Graph-paper ground at 24px, visible in both themes.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Each accent colour carries exactly one recurring meaning and is never used as general decoration. Magenta means act, cyan means information, green means nominal, red means fault, yellow means state/utility. A new accent role needs a new decision, not a reassignment.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Colour never communicates category or state by itself. Every coloured chip, badge, and tag ships a text label; the label carries the meaning and the colour only reinforces it.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: No text is set in an accent-on-accent or accent-on-paper combination. Ink on any accent is the default; the lowest ratio in the shipped set is magenta at 5.19:1, still above the 4.5:1 normal-text floor.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Data Rule
rules.body: Anything a machine would produce — timestamps, counts, reading time, identifiers, tags, status badges — is set in JetBrains Mono, uppercase, bold, at 0.75rem. Anything a human wrote is set in Inter or Space Grotesk. Never mix the two roles inside one element.

rules.name: The Uppercase Structure Rule
rules.body: All headings at Headline level and above are uppercase. Uppercase is what separates a heading from a sentence in this system; do not set a headline in sentence case.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: Hover always moves an element toward its shadow and shrinks the shadow; it never grows it, never blurs it, and never lifts the element off the page. The transition is translate(3px, 3px) with the shadow dropping one tier.

rules.name: The Zero-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in the system has a 0px blur radius and a 0px spread. Blur is banned; if depth needs to read stronger, increase the offset or the tier, not the softness.

rules.name: The Signal Word Rule
rules.body: A readout's tag states the state in words — Reading, Index, Query, No signal, Fault — and never appears as colour alone. The accent reinforces the word; it does not replace it.

rules.name: The Data Case Rule
rules.body: Readout chrome is uppercase mono, but a value the reader supplied or a real path keeps its own case: a requested path renders /blog/nope/, not /BLOG/NOPE/. Uppercase is for labels, never for data.

rules.name: The Instrument, Not Container Rule
rules.body: A readout marks a moment the visitor must read or act on. Do not wrap ordinary page content in one, and do not stack readouts; a page has one instrument or none.

rules.name: The Link Contrast Rule
rules.body: Prose links use the Alert Magenta Text tier (#E01281) in the light theme and full-chroma Alert Magenta (#FF1493) in the dark theme. Full-chroma magenta fails 4.5:1 on every light surface in this system; a link is text first and a signal second.

dos: Do bound every surface with a 2–4px Console Black rule. An unboxed surface is not part of this system.
Do use solid offset shadows from the Brutal XS/SM/MD/LG ladder with 0px blur, and move the element toward the shadow on hover.
Do keep every corner at 0 radius — buttons, cards, inputs, avatars, images, badges alike.
Do set machine-produced text (dates, counts, reading time, tags, badges) in uppercase JetBrains Mono at 0.75rem/700.
Do pair every accent colour with a text label; colour reinforces meaning, it never carries it alone.
Do set ink on accent, never accent on accent, and keep the pairing at or above 4.5:1.
Do use the 1180px shell and SectionContainer for page structure, and the 720px measure for article body.
Do report states through a console readout — a named signal tag plus the machine values — and keep the reader's own data in its original case.
donts: Don't introduce muted or low-contrast palettes — the confirmed rejection for this system. Calm comes from order and legibility, not desaturation.
Don't add blur to any shadow, or use a diffuse drop shadow in place of an offset one.
Don't round a corner, even by 2px, on any component.
Don't use gradients as fills. (The only gradient in the codebase is the unused .card::before hover border sweep, which is dead CSS and not part of the system.)
Don't lift an element on hover; hover presses toward the shadow, it never floats.
Don't use Alert Magenta as general decoration — it is the action colour and stays rationed.
Don't set body copy in Space Grotesk or headings in JetBrains Mono; the three families have fixed roles.
